status.note: Chosen to break the state model. A checkbox has THREE conditions — unchecked, checked, mixed — and every state in this schema so far has been a boolean. Sourced from the W3C ARIA APG checkbox pattern, which specifies the tri-state case normatively.

intent.purpose: Records a yes/no answer that is collected rather than acted on immediately, and can additionally report that a set of answers below it is partly yes.
behaviour: Holds one of three conditions: unchecked, checked, or mixed. Mixed is not a third user choice — a user can only move between checked and unchecked; mixed is what a parent reports when its children disagree.
Toggles between checked and unchecked on click, and on Space when focused. Activating a mixed checkbox resolves it to checked.
Shows a tick when checked and a dash when mixed. The two are different marks, not the same mark dimmed, because they mean different things.
Announces mixed as mixed, not as unchecked. A parent that says 'no' when three of five children say 'yes' is lying to anyone who cannot see the dash.
notFor: An immediate setting. A checkbox implies its answer is collected and applied later; a switch takes effect at once.
Choosing one of several options. That is a radio group, which enforces exactly one answer.
Being set to mixed by a user. Mixed is derived from the state of other checkboxes; offering it as a third click target confuses the meaning.

checked.description: The answer. Three values, not two: `mixed` reports that a set of checkboxes below this one is partly checked, and is set by the implementation rather than chosen by a user.
checked.visual: A tick when checked, a dash when mixed, an empty box when unchecked.

disabled.description: The platform's own disabled state. Removed from the focus order and cannot be answered.
disabled.visual: The box and its label dim, and the pointer cursor is dropped.

invalid.description: The answer failed validation — typically a required checkbox left unchecked.
invalid.visual: The box takes its error border.

hover.description: The pointer is over the checkbox and it is not disabled.
hover.visual: The box's border takes its hover treatment.

focus-visible.description: Focused in a way the browser judges worth showing a ring for — keyboard, not a mouse click.
focus-visible.visual: A ring is drawn around the box.

a11y.keyboard: Tab reaches it unless disabled. Space toggles between checked and unchecked; a mixed checkbox resolves to checked.
notes: `mixed` must reach assistive technology as `mixed` and not as unchecked. This is the whole reason the third value exists, and a boolean model cannot carry it.
The tick and the dash must be distinguishable by shape, not only by colour or weight. Anyone who cannot separate them is told 'some' when the answer is 'all'.
The accessible name is whatever is passed as the label. A checkbox with no label has no name, and nothing here detects that.
`disabled` removes it from the focus order, so a keyboard user cannot land on it to discover why it is unavailable.

label.description: The question being answered. Fills the `label` part.

root.description: The checkbox and its label, kept together so the whole row is the target.

box.description: The square. Owns the border, the focus ring and the fill, and holds whichever mark applies.

tick.description: The check mark. Shown only when the answer is a definite yes.

dash.description: The mixed mark. A different shape from the tick, not a dimmed one — it reports a different fact.
